key_insight: Cu feedstock morphology governs impact deformation in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ composites: spherical particles localize strain at splat boundaries, while spongy particles distribute strain through ligament collapse.
engineering_relevance: Powder morphology offers an additional design lever alongside spray parameters for tailoring composite microstructure and mechanical performance.
method: Compare deposits produced from spherical and spongy Cu feedstocks.
Characterize microstructure and measure nano- and micro-hardness.
Evaluate mechanical and tribological behavior using micro-compression and tribological tests.
evidence_signal: Multi-scale characterization links spherical Cu to bimodal grain structures and a strength–ductility balance, and spongy Cu to distributed strain hardening and enhanced ceramic encapsulation.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or processing window, limiting assessment of practical optimization and transferability.
paper_title: Feedstock Morphology Governs Impact-Induced Deformation in Cold Sprayed Metal-Ceramic Composites
